_comment: RB-011 probe manifest: durable, machine-checkable claims each register a re-verification command here so `node tools/dev/run-probes.js` can execute them all at orient. needsServer=true probes are skipped (not failed) when nothing serves :3170. Add an entry whenever a doc/memory claim gains a runnable check.

probes.description: Whole DB-frontier API surface healthy (P1-P6 endpoints)

fleet resolver + port inventory coherent (v2=3200 deployed, worker 8081, legacy 3120 orphaned) + Oracle v2 reachability surfaced informationally — the D1 guard against remote-config sprawl (2026-07-21, cycle 65)
churn-scan tool runs and produces JSON (RB-004)
timed-probe REFUSES an unbounded (no-LIMIT) query — the WAL-pin incident guard (expect exit 3)
dev-bridge heartbeat is fresh (bridge alive + processing) — surfaces a dead/wedged bridge at orient instead of silently piling up inbox actions

server-child resilience (supervisor + watchdog + FATAL capture) and run-multi dispatch-and-return wiring are present — a static tripwire so a refactor can't silently delete the crash/wedge guards (2026-07-20)

DELEGATABLE raw-SQL signatures outside ncdb do not exceed the ceiling — RATCHETED DOWN as delegations land (269 baseline → 258 → 249 schema-introspection helpers out of validate-url-normalization → 241 same helpers reused in normalize-fetches + normalize-place-hubs, 2026-07-21 → … → 195). SEMANTICS CHANGED 2026-08-05 (cycle 218), deliberately: the ceiling guarded the RAW total, which could be satisfied by DELETING code — c217's retirement of one unreachable file dropped it 195→182 and c218's owner-directed removal of three spent migrations took another 30, neither of which moved one query into ncdb. The guarded number is now the scan's DELEGATABLE count (reachable, non-excluded files: the SQL that could actually move), which held at 118 across both of those cleanups. Ceiling set to 118 = the measured delegatable count at the changeover, NOT a loosening. Lower it only when a delegation reduces the count; raise only deliberately

operational-UI files in the monorepo do not exceed the ceiling — the news-crawler-ui extraction ratchet (owner directive 2026-08-03, cycle 168; baseline 643 = tracked src/ui minus projectStatus, which stays as the loop's own instrument). Wins that lower it: a UI moved to ../news-crawler-ui with the monorepo copy DELETED, or a stale dir retired in place. Born from the module-ecosystem audit: the one extraction with a probe-enforced number (ncdb-debt) advanced while every prose-only extraction froze — a rule without an instrument decays

crawler-engine files in the monorepo do not exceed the ceiling — the news-crawler-itself extraction ratchet (owner-picked instrument, cycle 174; baseline 365 = tracked src/core/crawler, tests included since they move with their modules). Down = delegation-with-deletion into news-crawler-itself (rule 3: diff return shapes first) or reference-scanned retirement — and the scan must match relative require forms, the c171/c173 lesson. Constraint: the politeness gate points into this tree (DomainThrottleManager requiredPatterns); any slice moving it moves the gate config in the same commit. Born from the audit finding confirmed three times: instrumented extractions advance (ncdb 269→241, ui 643→488), prose-only ones freeze

every improvement cycle >= the instrumentation floor (47) carries a well-formed machine-readable `<!-- cycle:{...} -->` stanza under its ledger row (cost-per-improvement + recursion + coordination-debt series). Guards the loop's own measurement record against silent rot, the same way ncdb-debt-ratchet guards raw SQL. See docs/agi/WORKFLOW_MEASUREMENT.md (2026-07-21, cycle 47)

agent scope matches disk reality: every in-scope sibling repo exists, is versioned, and its origin matches its name (config/repo-scope.json vs the filesystem). Added 2026-07-27 after prose scope drifted twice: the module-ecosystem doc called news-crawler-itself 'an EMPTY placeholder' months after it held 36 files, and a .git-based survey silently skipped it BECAUSE it is unversioned — the case that most needed flagging. knownIssue entries WARN loudly every orient without failing

every cycle stanza parses AND carries well-typed fields (RB-015). The stanza is the loop's only act of record-keeping - the SVG, status page and next-prompt generator are projections of it, so one mistyped stanza corrupts every view at once. Placeholders (documentation naming the convention in prose) are excluded by the parser, which for several cycles miscounted them as 2 malformed stanzas - a parser defect, not a ledger defect

committed progress.svg is byte-identical to a fresh render from the current ledger + annotations (RB-015; determinism makes staleness an exact compare). Red mid-cycle after appending a ledger row is EXPECTED until the close-the-cycle regeneration runs; red at orient means the ritual was skipped last cycle

RB-008 instruction-compliance meta-test: the AGENT followed its standing directives, not just the code passing. Checks the close-the-cycle ritual actually completed (newest stanza committed at HEAD, record files clean, HEAD level with origin/main, repo-activity snapshot covers the newest stanza) plus owner-GATED directives a well-meaning agent could quietly violate: the crawler concurrency default (<= 3) and, since cycle 130, the STANDING gates that bind during a turn - hooks/skills installation, the two ~30 GB backups still existing, and the 429 backoff escalation not being weakened, all baselined in config/gated-surfaces.json - plus the verify-honestly paper trail (every stanza records a verification[]). It also PRINTS the directives it cannot check (prompt regeneration, whether BOOT.md was read, agent-vs-crawler live-DB writes) so a green line never reads as fuller coverage than it is. Added cycle 128 after the c127 lanes revealed cycles 47-120 landed as bulk catch-up commits days after their ledger dates - the commit step was being deferred invisibly because nothing checked the agent, only the artifacts. A1-A3 red MID-CYCLE is the ritual in progress; red at ORIENT means last cycle skipped a step

the three CODE CONTRACTS the progress picture and status page depend on (RB-011, cycle 131): P1 progress-svg.js reads only COMMITTED inputs, never live git (the staleness byte-compare is only sound while the render is pure); P2 the status page's client fetches IMMEDIATELY on activate, not only on an interval (the jsgui3 Server({Ctrl}) recipe publishes SSR once at server start, so without it every visitor reads boot-time numbers - this guards the c128.5 fix, which shipped unguarded); P3 /progress.svg is read from disk INSIDE its route handler so a regenerated picture appears without a redeploy. Unlike progress-svg-staleness these should NEVER be red - kept a separate probe precisely so 'red is expected mid-cycle' stays unambiguous. Deliberately NOT probed: jsgui3's own publish-once behaviour (a consume-only dependency's internals)

the handful of UI checks that drive a REAL browser cannot silently drop to zero (RB-009, cycle 133). Measured 2026-07-27: of 82 UI self-tests totalling ~10,600 lines, only 4 (5%) drive puppeteer/playwright; 75 (91%) are in-process render + string assertions. That 95% majority is blind BY CONSTRUCTION to the cycle-128.5 defect class - SSR frozen at publish while the client silently repairs the DOM, so the page looks correct to every string assertion. This is a no-regression FLOOR, raised deliberately as live coverage lands: 4 -> 5 in cycle 135. LOWERED 5 -> 4 in cycle 212: the fifth was a LAB check, and the jsgui3 research lab moved to the sibling repo ../jsgui3-experiments by owner ruling in cycle 208 — those puppeteer checks still exist and run there. This is a RELOCATION, not lost coverage; the monorepo's four operational browser checks are unchanged, when projectStatus.live.check.js became the first check in the tree to load a real page in a real browser (the 3 pre-existing screenshot checks render SSR HTML in-process and photograph it, so they never load a URL either)

every markdown link in the LIVING doc corpus (docs/agi) resolves (RB-003, cycle 134). Scoped deliberately: the 154-doc legacy docs/ corpus is 94% frozen 2025 point-in-time analyses, and 'aligning' a dated architecture review with today's code would destroy the record it exists to be - so no diffing strategy was built, only this guard on the corpus BOOT actually depends on. Measured contradiction across both corpora was 13 broken links in 172 docs; the 2 in docs/agi are fixed. Only markdown links are checked: an earlier pass that counted backticked filenames reported 982 broken refs at a 98.7% false-positive rate

loads the project-status page in a REAL browser and asserts the five things no in-process check can see (cycle 135): L1 the isomorphic client actually activated, L2 it fetched /api/status ON LOAD rather than only on the 60 s interval (guards the c128.5 fix), L3 the rendered DOM agrees with the LIVE API rather than the boot-time SSR - the assertion that would have failed automatically in c128.5 when SSR said 82 cycles and the API said 84 - L4 no console errors, L5 every page-requested resource loaded. Spawns its own server on :3191 so a running preview on :3184 is untouched, and uses async spawn (spawnSync would deadlock the event loop the server needs). Proven to bite: removing the c128.5 one-line fix turns L2 red

loads the Crawl Console (news-crawler-ui, the UI-split founding consumer) in a REAL browser at orient: spawns its own runner on :3195 against the live news.db READ-ONLY, then runs the module's own checks/console.live.check.js — activation, on-load fetch, DOM-vs-API liveness agreement, durable content (policy hosts + the owner-gated politeness line + the launcher), zero console errors, and COMPUTED-STYLE application (cycle 169: the page once served 39 bytes of collected css and rendered unstyled while eleven text assertions passed). Readiness budget 90s covers the documented bundle-publish boot (the cycle-169 probe-flake lesson). Expected strings are durable facts, not day-fresh data

the owner's big-lightbulb research signal (cycle 139): a click on a signal-bearing tech node POSTs to the status server, which appends a pending record to data/agi-signals.jsonl. RED here is not breakage - it is the OWNER TALKING: orient cannot pass until the requested research is taken up and acknowledged (node tools/agi/ack-signal.js <id> "note"). The same pending records render as a ⚡ OWNER SIGNAL line above the ▶ selection in the generated next-prompt, so the click reaches the agent on both surfaces it provably reads every cycle

the tech-tree spec (config/tech-tree.json) builds cleanly against the live backlog (cycle 147, shipped by the first owner-signalled TECH-APPREVIEW run). buildTechTree THROWS on a phantom edge / third prereq / unknown branch / curated tech claiming completion - but only at page render; this probe runs the same build at orient, the same promotion stanza-schema made for ledger records. A growing hand-edited JSON deserves a machine check before anyone reads it

zombie crawl-state tripwire on the Oracle box (task #70, cycle 151): RED when domain states claim 'running' while the orchestrator reports nothing running and throughput is zero — the exact signature that sat unnoticed for 6.8 days on 2026-07-28 (totals.fetched frozen at 12 against a 10,048 queue) hiding a dead crawl AND falsely blocking deploys. Uses the deploy tool's own classifyBusyStatus so probe and busy-gate can never disagree about the signature. With the engine's heartbeat-loss transition deployed, zombies self-heal in ~2 min, so a persistent red = that fix regressed or a new stale-state class. An unreachable box is NOT red here (reachability belongs to remote-endpoints)

no workflow task-type with >=5 recorded runs exceeds the cost-to-catch ceiling (turns spent per validation-CONFIRMED real catch) — a degrading/bloating workflow surface (one that stops earning its cost) is a regression, caught at orient. Bootstrapped 2026-07-21 (cycle 48) with 13 labeled runs; diagnosis=0.9, delegation-safety=1.0, equivalence=0.4. See docs/agi/WORKFLOW_MEASUREMENT.md §2 (cost-to-catch is the sound ratchet signal; verdict-accuracy is a diagnostic-to-read, not a gate, because a REFUTED verdict can be the workflow correctly refuting a bad premise)

no test file carries an unresolvable require()/jest.mock() target (the never-ran-suite class that bit three times: utils.safeCall c177, milestoneTracker c181, enhanced-features c182). Sweeps EVERY *.test.js in BOTH repos and resolves every string-literal edge against the real tree; ratchets down from the measured 16 (cycle 183) toward zero. Caught its own builder on first run: the two cycle-183 travelled tests carried self-name requires jest resolves but raw Node rejects

the crawler suite failing-set is PINNED BY NAME (set-shrink-only, tools/dev/checks/known-failures.json) — quick mode validates registry hygiene at orient; --verify (cycle-close, whenever src/core/crawler changes) runs the scoped suite and fails on any failing suite not in the registry. Replaces the memorized known-51; baseline 17 suites / 49 tests after the c184 placeHubs real-defect fix

components with file-config fallbacks actually loaded their REAL config (c188 lesson: CategoryClassifier served its 35-keyword ENOENT fallback in production for months, warning into unwatched logs — a fallback that degrades quietly is a defect with a delay timer). Constructs each registered component at orient and asserts real-config markers (classifier: phrases>=10, keywords>=100)

key entry modules require() cleanly under raw Node, each in a child process (c191 lesson: the c181 extraction left ONE dangling require in IntelligentPlanRunner and NewsCrawler + the legacy CLI were unloadable for FIVE cycles — invisible because the v1 API builds crawls from engine parts and the phantom sweep scans only test files). NewsCrawler, IntelligentPlanRunner, CrawlOperations, crawlService, CrawlerServiceWiring

BARE (uncommented) silent catches ratchet down from the measured 378 (cycle 197 survey: 859 silent catches total across 347 files, both repos — commented ones are reviewed decisions and legal; bare ones are unreviewed swallows, the class that produced or hid FOUR production defects: recordUrlAlias, the 4%-keyword-base classifier fallback, the Readability fallback, swallowed hierarchy writes). Convert each bare swallow to a loud warn or a commented decision — never delete the catch unread
